title: Certification Decoder
summary: A label is only as good as the standard behind it. Search a certification, seal, or logo you have seen on a product and find out who runs it, what it actually verifies, and — just as importantly — what it does not.

schemes.name: Leaping Bunny
schemes.verifies: No animal testing at any stage — finished product AND ingredients — by the brand, its suppliers, or third parties, with a fixed cut-off date and independent audits plus supplier monitoring.
schemes.notguarantee: Does NOT mean vegan. A Leaping Bunny product can still contain animal-derived ingredients (beeswax, lanolin, carmine).
schemes.src: Cruelty Free International / Leaping Bunny Programme.

schemes.name: PETA — Beauty Without Bunnies
schemes.verifies: Brand has signed a statement of assurance that it and its suppliers do not test on animals. Two logos exist: ‘Animal Test-Free’ and ‘Animal Test-Free & Vegan’.
schemes.notguarantee: The standard base logo relies on a signed pledge rather than independent audit, and the test-free-only logo does not mean vegan.

schemes.name: Certified Vegan (Vegan Society / Vegan Action)
schemes.verifies: No animal-derived ingredients and no animal testing by the company. The sunflower trademark requires an application and ingredient review.
schemes.notguarantee: ‘Vegan’ alone (uncertified) is unregulated. Vegan does not automatically mean cruelty-free unless the certifier also covers testing.

schemes.name: RSPCA Assured
schemes.verifies: Farm-animal welfare against RSPCA species-specific standards, covering the animal’s life, transport, and slaughter, with assessment visits.
schemes.notguarantee: It is a welfare scheme, not organic or free-range by default, and does not mean the animal was not killed.

schemes.name: Certified Humane
schemes.verifies: Farm-animal welfare standards including space, no cages for hens, and no routine antibiotics, with annual third-party inspection.
schemes.notguarantee: A welfare label, not a ‘no-slaughter’ label; standards differ from organic and from country-specific free-range definitions.

schemes.name: RSPO
schemes.verifies: Palm oil produced to RSPO criteria on a certified plantation. ‘Segregated’ and ‘Identity Preserved’ are the strongest supply-chain models.
schemes.notguarantee: Weaker models (‘Mass Balance’, ‘Book & Claim’/credits) mean certified and non-certified oil may be mixed. RSPO has faced criticism over deforestation in member supply chains.

schemes.name: GOTS
schemes.verifies: Textiles with a minimum 70% certified organic fibre PLUS environmental and social criteria (banned toxic inputs, wastewater treatment, workers’ rights) across the whole supply chain.
schemes.notguarantee: ‘Made with organic’ (70–94%) is a lower grade than the ‘organic’ grade (95%+). Organic cotton still uses significant water.

schemes.name: OEKO-TEX Standard 100
schemes.verifies: That the finished textile has been tested for a list of harmful substances and is below defined limits — a chemical-safety label for the end product.
schemes.notguarantee: It is NOT an organic, animal-welfare, labour, or environmental-footprint standard. It only addresses substances in the tested article.

schemes.name: Fairtrade
schemes.verifies: Producers received the Fairtrade Minimum Price and a Fairtrade Premium, with standards on labour rights and environmental practice, independently audited by FLOCERT.
schemes.notguarantee: Covers the certified ingredient(s), not necessarily the whole product; on composite products a percentage applies. Not an organic or animal-welfare label.

schemes.name: B Corp
schemes.verifies: The whole COMPANY passed a verified assessment of its social and environmental performance, accountability, and transparency (minimum score 80), re-certified every three years.
schemes.notguarantee: It rates the company overall — not any single product, and not specifically animal welfare or veganism. A B Corp can still sell products you might avoid.

schemes.name: FSC
schemes.verifies: Wood, paper, or forest-derived material comes from responsibly managed forests meeting FSC environmental and social standards, tracked by chain-of-custody.
schemes.notguarantee: ‘FSC Mix’ blends certified, recycled, and ‘controlled’ material — not 100% certified. Look for ‘FSC 100%’ for the strongest claim.

schemes.name: Soil Association Organic
schemes.verifies: Organic certification for food, and a separate strict standard for organic health & beauty covering ingredients, GM-free, and (for beauty) no animal testing.
schemes.notguarantee: Organic addresses how something is grown/made, not animal-welfare outcomes or whether an animal was killed.

schemes.name: USDA Organic / EU Organic Leaf
schemes.verifies: Food produced under legally-defined organic rules: no synthetic pesticides/fertilisers, no GMOs, and defined animal-welfare and feed rules for livestock.
schemes.notguarantee: Organic is not automatically ‘free-range’ nor a guarantee of high welfare beyond the baseline rules; it is not a cruelty-free or vegan label.

schemes.name: Rainforest Alliance
schemes.verifies: Farms (coffee, cocoa, tea, bananas) met standards on forests, climate, human rights, and livelihoods, audited against the 2020 Sustainable Agriculture Standard.
schemes.notguarantee: Uses mass-balance for cocoa (certified and non-certified can be mixed) and has faced scrutiny over on-the-ground enforcement.

schemes.name: Fair Wear Foundation
schemes.verifies: That a clothing brand is a member working to improve labour conditions in its supply chain, assessed on its practices (a ‘Brand Performance Check’).
schemes.notguarantee: It rates the brand’s EFFORT and management, not a pass/fail guarantee that every factory is perfect. Not an environmental or animal label.
schemes.src: Fair Wear Foundation Code of Labour Practices.

schemes.name: Responsible Down / Wool Standard (RDS / RWS)
schemes.verifies: Down or wool traced through the supply chain with animal-welfare criteria — RDS prohibits live-plucking and force-feeding; RWS addresses sheep welfare and land management.
schemes.notguarantee: It improves welfare within animal use; it does not mean no animal was farmed or slaughtered. Mulesing is prohibited under RWS but check the specific claim.

schemes.name: Global Recycled Standard (GRS)
schemes.verifies: Tracks recycled content through the supply chain (minimum 20% to carry the logo, 50%+ for full claims), plus social and environmental criteria at each stage.
schemes.notguarantee: Does NOT mean the whole garment is recycled, or that it is low-impact overall — only that the certified recycled content is genuine and traceable.

schemes.name: bluesign
schemes.verifies: Manages chemical inputs across textile manufacturing — restricting hazardous substances and improving resource use at the factory level.
schemes.notguarantee: Does NOT address animal welfare or garment-worker wages; it is a chemical and environmental management system, not an ethics-of-labour mark.

schemes.name: Cradle to Cradle Certified
schemes.runby: Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute
schemes.verifies: Assesses products across material health, reuse, renewable energy, water, and social fairness, at Bronze–Platinum levels.
schemes.notguarantee: A low tier (Bronze) is a much weaker claim than Gold/Platinum — the level matters, and the logo alone doesn’t tell you which.
schemes.src: Cradle to Cradle Products Innovation Institute.

schemes.name: Fair Trade Certified (US)
schemes.verifies: Sets standards for wages, safe conditions, and community funds for producers; distinct from Fairtrade International (different standards and governance).
schemes.notguarantee: Does NOT certify the whole company — only specific certified products or facilities; the rest of the brand may be unaudited.

schemes.name: ZQ Merino
schemes.verifies: Wool standard covering animal welfare (including non-mulesing), environmental management, and social responsibility on accredited farms.
schemes.notguarantee: Applies to the certified wool fibre, not the finished garment’s full supply chain (dyeing, sewing, labour elsewhere).

schemes.name: Regenerative Organic Certified (ROC)
schemes.verifies: Builds on organic certification with added requirements for soil health, animal welfare, and farmworker fairness — one of the stricter farm-level marks.
schemes.notguarantee: Still farm-level: it certifies how a raw material was grown, not how the final product was manufactured or by whom.
